result.topic_en: Euler substitutes particular arcs into a trigonometric series summing to πω/4 and integrates the derived cosine series to sum 1 − 1/3³ + 1/5³ − … ; in Scholion 2 (§23) he puts Φ = π and Φ = 2π into a general relation, resolves the apparent contradiction between the two results, and expresses the series sum as a double integral, comparing it with π/sin nπ ∫xⁿdx(1−x)ⁿ⁻¹.
result.transcription:
174

Sit autem $\omega = \frac{\pi}{2}$, oriturque series etiam cognita
$\frac{\pi\pi}{8} = \frac{1}{1} + \frac{1}{9} + \frac{1}{25} + \frac{1}{49} + \frac{1}{81} + $ etc.
At sumto arcu $\omega = 45^\circ = \frac{\pi}{4}$, prodiit
$\frac{\pi\pi}{8\sqrt{2}} = 1 - \frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{25} + \frac{1}{49} + \frac{1}{81} - \frac{1}{121} - \frac{1}{169} + $ etc.
Sit $\omega = 30^\circ = \frac{\pi}{6}$, erit
$\frac{\pi\pi}{24} = \frac{1}{2}(1 + \frac{1}{49} + \frac{1}{169} + \frac{1}{361} + \frac{1}{625} + \frac{1}{961} + $ etc.)
$- 1(\frac{1}{9} + \frac{1}{81} + \frac{1}{225} + \frac{1}{441} + $ etc.)
$+ \frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{25} + \frac{1}{121} + \frac{1}{289} + \frac{1}{529} + \frac{1}{841} + $ etc.)
ubi media est $= \frac{\pi\pi}{72}$, reliquarumque ratio perspicua. Deinde differentiatio nostrae seriei suppeditat hanc formam notatu dignam:
$\frac{\pi}{4} = \cos.\omega - \frac{1}{3}\cos.3\omega + \frac{1}{5}\cos.5\omega - \frac{1}{7}\cos.7\omega + $ etc.
quoniam omnes plane arcus pro $\omega$ assumti eandem praebent summam. Tum vero iterata differentiatio praebet:
$0 = \sin.\omega - \sin.3\omega + \sin.5\omega - \sin.7\omega + $ etc.
Per integrationem autem elicimus:
$C - \frac{\pi\omega^2}{8} = \cos.\omega - \frac{1}{27}\cos.3\omega + \frac{1}{125}\cos.5\omega - \frac{1}{343}\cos.7\omega + $ etc.
ubi cum sumto $\omega = 0$ fit $1 - \frac{1}{3^3} + \frac{1}{5^3} - \frac{1}{7^3} + $ etc. $= \frac{\pi^3}{32}$, erit
$C = \frac{\pi^3}{32}$, ita ut sit
$\frac{\pi}{8}(\frac{\pi\pi}{4} - \omega\omega) = \cos.\omega - \frac{1}{3^3}\cos.3\omega + \frac{1}{5^3}\cos.5\omega - \frac{1}{7^3}\cos.7\omega + $ etc.

Scholion 2.

§. 23. Ponamus nunc in genere $\Phi = \pi$, et cum sit $\sin.(n+1)\pi = -\sin.n\pi$; $\sin.(n+2)\pi = +\sin.n\pi$; etc. aequatio nostra per $\sin.n\pi$ divisa induet hanc formam:
$\frac{\pi}{\sin.n\pi}\int x^n dx(1-x)^{n-1} = \frac{1}{n^2} + \frac{2n}{1(n+1)^2} + \frac{2n(2n+1)}{1.2(n+2)^2} + \frac{2n(2n+1)(2n+2)}{1.2.3(n+3)^2} + $ etc.
sumto

175

sumto autem $\Phi = 2\pi$, erit simili modo:
$\frac{2\pi}{\sin.2n\pi}\int x^n dx(1-x)^{n-1} = \frac{1}{n^2} - \frac{2n}{1(n+1)^2} + \frac{2n(2n+1)}{1.2(n+2)^2} - \frac{2n(2n+1)(2n+2)}{1.2.3(n+3)^2} + $ etc.
quarum serierum ergo illa per hanc divisa quotum praebet $= \cos.n\pi$, quod incongruum videtur, cum quotus sit unitate maior. At similem difficultatem iam supra resolvimus, quae ex positione $\Phi = 2\pi$ est nata: si enim poneremus $\Phi = 3\pi$, ipsa series prior emergeret, summam habitura $= \frac{3\pi}{\sin.3n\pi}\int x^n dx(1-x)^{n-1}$, quae illi non est aequalis, nisi $n$ sit ratio evanescens. Quare prima tantum series locum habere est censenda, cuius summam ut ex ipsa eius natura investigemus, statuamus:
$s = \frac{1}{n^2}t^n + \frac{2n}{(n+1)^2}t^{n+1} + \frac{2n(2n+1)}{1.2(n+2)^2}t^{n+2} + $ etc.
eritque hinc
$\frac{d.t\,ds}{dt^2} = 1t^{n-1} + \frac{2n}{1}t^n + \frac{2n(2n+1)}{1.2}t^{n+1} + $ etc.
cuius seriei summa manifesto est $= t^{n-1}(1-t)^{-2n}$, ita ut
$\frac{t\,ds}{dt} = \int t^{n-1}dt(1-t)^{-2n}$ et
$s = \int\frac{dt}{t}\int\frac{t^{n-1}dt}{(1-t)^{2n}}$,
sicque posito post integrationem $t = 1$ habebitur:
$\frac{\pi}{\sin.n\pi}\int x^n dx(1-x)^{n-1} = \int\frac{dt}{t}\int\frac{t^{n-1}dt}{(1-t)^{2n}}$.
Quae binarum formularum integralium comparatio eo magis est memorabilis, quod inter plurimas alias, quae adhuc sunt erutae, huius generis non reperiantur.

items.english: Dividing the former of these series by the latter therefore gives the quotient cos nπ, which seems inconsistent, since the quotient is greater than one.

items.english: Therefore only the first series should be considered valid.
